keyTakeaways: A Tamil wish takes one of three shapes: the noun நல்வாழ்த்துகள் (good wishes), the optative -க (வாழ்க, may you flourish) or the "let it" form -கட்டும் (ஒளிரட்டும், let it shine).
The Tamil Lexicon (p. 3620) defines வாழ்த்து as "benediction, felicitation", built on வாழ், "to live, to flourish".
Blessings travel from elder to younger: wish an elder with நீங்கள் and ask for their ஆசி (Lexicon p. 211) rather than saying வாழ்க.
Tamil Deepavali is Thursday 28 October 2027 per Drik Panchang, a day before North India's Friday 29 October.
On Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89, SubhSandesh's nearest festival data), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the day itself.

faqs.question: What is the most common way to write Deepavali wishes in Tamil?
faqs.answer: The standard written form is இனிய தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள் (iṉiya tīpāvaḷi nalvāḻttukaḷ), roughly "sweet Deepavali, good wishes". It is neutral, so it works for anyone from a colleague to a grandparent.

faqs.question: What does vazhthukkal mean?
faqs.answer: வாழ்த்துகள் is the plural of வாழ்த்து, which the Tamil Lexicon (p. 3620) defines as "benediction, felicitation" and "praise". It comes from வாழ், "to live, to flourish", so a vāḻttu is a wish that someone lives well.

faqs.question: How do I wish my grandparents for Deepavali in Tamil?
faqs.answer: Use the respectful நீங்கள் form and ask for their blessing rather than giving one, for example "இந்த தீபாவளிக்கும் என்னை ஆசீர்வதியுங்கள்" (bless me this Deepavali too). In Tamil families the blessing travels from elder to younger.

faqs.question: Can a younger person say வாழ்க to an elder?
faqs.answer: It is better avoided. வாழ்க (may you flourish) is the shape of a blessing, which an elder gives; a younger person wishing an elder usually says they bow (வணங்குகிறேன்) and asks for the elder's ஆசி.

faqs.question: What is the difference between ஒளிர்க and ஒளிரட்டும்?
faqs.answer: Both mean "may it shine". ஒளிர்க (oḷirka) is the optative, formal and a little literary; ஒளிரட்டும் (oḷiraṭṭum) is the "let it" form, warmer and closer to how people talk.

faqs.question: Is Tamil Deepavali on 28 or 29 October 2027?
faqs.answer: Drik Panchang lists Tamil Deepavali on Thursday 28 October 2027 and North Indian Deepavali on Friday 29 October. Some holiday lists print 29 October for Tamil Nadu, and the state's 2027 order was not out as of October 2026, so wish on the 28th and check the holiday separately.

faqs.question: How do I type Deepavali wishes in Tamil on my phone?
faqs.answer: Add a Tamil keyboard in your phone's language settings, or type the Roman version and let a transliteration keyboard convert it. If the reader does not read Tamil script, send the Roman line as it is.

faqs.question: How should I spell Tamil wishes in English letters?
faqs.answer: In a chat, drop the diacritics and write ḻ as zh, so vāḻttukaḷ becomes vazhthukal. The dotted letters in this post (ḻ, ṟ, ṉ, ḷ) are there only so the pronunciation is exact.

faqs.question: Is there a Tirukkural couplet about lamps for Deepavali?
faqs.answer: Couplet 299, எல்லா விளக்கும் விளக்கல்ல சான்றோர்க்குப் பொய்யா விளக்கே விளக்கு, says that not every lamp is a lamp and that to the wise only the lamp of truth counts. It is from the chapter on truthfulness, not about Deepavali, so present it as a classical line, not a festival verse.

faqs.question: What should I write if I forgot to send a Deepavali wish in Tamil?
faqs.answer: Own it lightly: "நேற்று வாழ்த்தத் தவறினேன்; இன்றும் விளக்கு எரிகிறது, அதனால் வாழ்த்தும் செல்லும்!" (I missed wishing you yesterday; the lamp is still burning, so the wish still counts). With Tamil and North Indian dates a day apart in 2027, the 29th is still festival time for many.

faqs.question: Can I write a Tamil wish on the SubhSandesh Diwali card?
faqs.answer: Yes, every line on the Happy Diwali card is editable, including the wish diyas and the letter. Tamil rendering has not been tested on every phone, so press Save and preview it on your own phone before you publish.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Deepavali Wishes in Tamil: 15 Original Lines, Each Word Checked

Deepavali wishes in Tamil come in three shapes: a greeting noun (இனிய தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள், iṉiya tīpāvaḷi nalvāḻttukaḷ, "sweet Deepavali, good wishes"), a blessing verb ending in -க (வாழ்க, "may you flourish") and a "let it be" ending in -கட்டும். Below are 15 original lines in Tamil script, Roman transliteration and English, sorted by who receives them, with the key words checked in the University of Madras *Tamil Lexicon*.

Write yours before the morning. SubhSandesh has no Deepavali data yet; on Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival we measured (n = 89 pages, a different one-day festival), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the day itself and 27.0% the day before. And 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so every line here fits on one screen.

## Three shapes of a Tamil wish, in the Tamil Lexicon (p. 3620)

Every Tamil wish rests on வாழ்த்து (vāḻttu). The [Tamil Lexicon defines வாழ்த்து on p. 3620](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%B5%E0%AE%BE%E0%AE%B4%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%A4%E0%AF%81&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) as "benediction, felicitation", then "praise", and builds it on வாழ், "to live, to flourish". A vāḻttu is, at root, a wish that someone lives well.

Tamil turns that root into three forms, and the one you pick sets the tone. All three appear below:

- **Noun + -கள்:** நல்வாழ்த்துகள் (nalvāḻttukaḷ), "good wishes". Neutral and safe for anyone.
- **Verb + -க, the optative:** வாழ்க (vāḻka), ஒளிர்க (oḷirka), "may you flourish", "may it shine". Formal; the shape of a blessing.
- **Verb + -கட்டும், "let it":** ஒளிரட்டும் (oḷiraṭṭum), "let it shine". Warm and conversational.

## Who blesses whom: the direction rule for elders (p. 211)

In a Tamil family the blessing travels downward. The [Lexicon glosses ஆசி (āci, p. 211)](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%86%E0%AE%9A%E0%AE%BF&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact) as "blessing, benediction" with வாழ்த்து as its synonym, and it is the elder who gives it: a grandmother says நீடூழி வாழ்க, "live for long ages", to a grandchild.

A younger person wishing an elder asks for that blessing instead, uses the respectful நீங்கள் (nīṅkaḷ) form and often says they bow (வணங்குகிறேன், vaṇaṅkukiṟēṉ). English "bless you" has no direction, so this is an easy slip in translation.

## Deepavali wishes in Tamil for parents and grandparents (3 lines, நீங்கள்)

All three use the respectful plural and ask rather than grant. Swap in your family's names.

- **அம்மா, அப்பா, இந்த தீபாவளி அன்று உங்கள் ஆசி மட்டுமே எனக்கு வேண்டும்.** (Ammā, Appā, inta tīpāvaḷi aṉṟu uṅkaḷ āci maṭṭumē eṉakku vēṇṭum.) "Amma, Appa, on this Deepavali your blessing is all I want."
- **பாட்டி, நீங்கள் ஏற்றிய விளக்கின் ஒளியில்தான் நான் வளர்ந்தேன்; இந்த தீபாவளிக்கும் என்னை ஆசீர்வதியுங்கள்.** (Pāṭṭi, nīṅkaḷ ēṟṟiya viḷakkiṉ oḷiyiltāṉ nāṉ vaḷarntēṉ; inta tīpāvaḷikkum eṉṉai ācīrvatiyuṅkaḷ.) "Paati, I grew up in the light of the lamps you lit; bless me this Deepavali too."
- **தூரத்தில் இருந்தாலும் உங்கள் காலைத் தொட்டு வணங்குகிறேன்; இனிய தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள்.** (Tūrattil iruntālum uṅkaḷ kālait toṭṭu vaṇaṅkukiṟēṉ; iṉiya tīpāvaḷi nalvāḻttukaḷ.) "Though I am far away, I touch your feet and bow; happy Deepavali."

## For friends, brothers and sisters (4 lines, நீ)

Between equals the informal நீ (nī) is warmer. Use it only where நீ already runs both ways.

- **நண்பா, ஊருக்கு வந்தால் நம் தெருவில் ஒரு விளக்கு உனக்காகவே எரியும்.** (Naṇpā, ūrukku vantāl nam teruvil oru viḷakku uṉakkākavē eriyum.) "Nanba, if you come home, one lamp on our street will burn just for you."
- **தங்கச்சி, உன் கோலம் போல் உன் வாழ்க்கையும் வண்ணமாக மலரட்டும்.** (Taṅkacci, uṉ kōlam pōl uṉ vāḻkkaiyum vaṇṇamāka malaraṭṭum.) "Thangachi, may your life bloom in colour, like your kolam."
- **அண்ணா, இந்த வருடம் புதுத்துணி நான் வாங்கித் தருகிறேன்; நீ இனிப்பு மட்டும் கொண்டு வா.** (Aṇṇā, inta varuṭam pututtuṇi nāṉ vāṅkit tarukiṟēṉ; nī iṉippu maṭṭum koṇṭu vā.) "Anna, this year I'll buy the new clothes; you just bring the sweets."
- **இருள் விலகுக, இனிமை பெருகுக, நம் நட்பு என்றும் ஒளிர்க!** (Iruḷ vilakuka, iṉimai perukuka, nam naṭpu eṉṟum oḷirka!) "May the dark withdraw, may sweetness grow, may our friendship always shine!"

## For a husband, wife or partner (3 lines)

Deepavali night falls on அமாவாசை (amāvācai), the new moon (Lexicon p. 104), which is why the third line has no moon in it. Pick the one that sounds like you.

- **என் வீட்டின் எல்லா விளக்குகளையும் விட, நீ ஏற்றும் அந்த ஒரு அகல்விளக்குதான் எனக்கு தீபாவளி.** (Eṉ vīṭṭiṉ ellā viḷakkukaḷaiyum viṭa, nī ēṟṟum anta oru akalviḷakkutāṉ eṉakku tīpāvaḷi.) "More than every lamp in my house, the one clay lamp you light is Deepavali to me."
- **கண்ணே, காலை நான்கு மணிக்கு என்னை எழுப்பும் உன் குரலே என் தீபாவளி இசை.** (Kaṇṇē, kālai nāṉku maṇikku eṉṉai eḻuppum uṉ kuralē eṉ tīpāvaḷi icai.) "Kanne, your voice waking me at four in the morning is my Deepavali music."
- **நீ துபாயில், நான் திருச்சியில்; இன்று இரவு ஒரே நிலவில்லா வானத்தின் கீழ் இருவரும் விளக்கு ஏற்றுவோம்.** (Nī Tupāyil, nāṉ Tirucciyil; iṉṟu iravu orē nilavillā vāṉattiṉ kīḻ iruvarum viḷakku ēṟṟuvōm.) "You in Dubai, me in Trichy; tonight we both light a lamp under the same moonless sky."

If your spouse is the one in Dubai this year, SubhSandesh's [miss-you page with a reunion countdown](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) may suit better. It is a romantic template, not a Deepavali one, and 28.0% of its senders set a reunion date (60 of 214).

## For colleagues and the family group (2 lines)

Group messages take அனைவருக்கும் (aṉaivarukkum, "to everyone") and the plural imperative. Keep the office line impersonal.

- **நம் குழுவின் அனைவருக்கும், அவர்கள் குடும்பத்தினருக்கும் இனிய தீபாவளி நல்வாழ்த்துகள்; இந்த ஆண்டின் உழைப்புக்கு நன்றி.** (Nam kuḻuviṉ aṉaivarukkum, avarkaḷ kuṭumpattiṉarukkum iṉiya tīpāvaḷi nalvāḻttukaḷ; inta āṇṭiṉ uḻaippukku naṉṟi.) "Happy Deepavali to everyone on our team and their families; thank you for this year's work."
- **நம் குடும்பக் குழுவில் இன்று எல்லோரும் ஒரு புகைப்படம் அனுப்புங்கள்; யார் வீட்டு விளக்கு வரிசை நீளம் என்று பார்ப்போம்!** (Nam kuṭumpak kuḻuvil iṉṟu ellōrum oru pukaippaṭam aṉuppuṅkaḷ; yār vīṭṭu viḷakku varicai nīḷam eṉṟu pārppōm!) "Everyone in the family group, send one photo today; let's see whose row of lamps is longest!"

## Blessings for children, and one belated line (3 lines)

These run the other way: an elder gives, so the verbs are optatives. The last is for the day after.

- **கண்ணு, நீடூழி வாழ்க; படிப்பும் பண்பும் விளக்குப் போல் ஒளிர்க.** (Kaṇṇu, nīṭūḻi vāḻka; paṭippum paṇpum viḷakkup pōl oḷirka.) "Kannu, live long; may your learning and your character shine like a lamp."
- **மகனே, நீ இருக்கும் ஊரில் விளக்கு ஏற்ற இடம் இல்லையென்றாலும், உன் பெயரில் இங்கே ஒன்று ஏற்றுகிறோம்.** (Makaṉē, nī irukkum ūril viḷakku ēṟṟa iṭam illaiyeṉṟālum, uṉ peyaril iṅkē oṉṟu ēṟṟukiṟōm.) "Son, even if there is no place to light a lamp where you live, we are lighting one here in your name."
- **நேற்று வாழ்த்தத் தவறினேன்; இன்றும் விளக்கு எரிகிறது, அதனால் வாழ்த்தும் செல்லும்!** (Nēṟṟu vāḻttat tavaṟiṉēṉ; iṉṟum viḷakku erikiṟatu, ataṉāl vāḻttum cellum!) "I missed wishing you yesterday; the lamp is still burning today, so the wish still counts!"

## Tirukkural couplet 299: a classical line about the lamp

For one line nobody can call a forward, quote Tiruvalluvar. Couplet 299 sits in the chapter on truthfulness; the [Project Madurai e-text of the Tirukkural](https://www.projectmadurai.org/pm_etexts/utf8/pmuni0001.html) gives it as below; the *Tamil Lexicon* also quotes its opening under [விளக்கு, "lamp, light" (p. 3725)](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/tamil-lex_query.py?qs=%E0%AE%B5%E0%AE%BF%E0%AE%B3%E0%AE%95%E0%AF%8D%E0%AE%95%E0%AF%81&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact). It suits a photo of one diya, or a teacher.

> **எல்லா விளக்கும் விளக்கல்ல சான்றோர்க்குப் பொய்யா விளக்கே விளக்கு.** (Ellā viḷakkum viḷakkalla cāṉṟōrkkup poyyā viḷakkē viḷakku.) "Not every lamp is a lamp; to the wise, the lamp that does not lie is the only lamp." Tiruvalluvar, *Tirukkural* 299; the English is our own rendering.

## When to send each line in Diwali week 2027

Tamil Nadu and North India split in 2027. [Drik Panchang's Tamil Deepavali page](https://www.drikpanchang.com/tamil/festivals/tamil-deepavali/tamil-deepavali-date-time.html?year=2027) puts Deepavali on Thursday 28 October 2027 and North Indian Deepavali on Friday 29 October,; some 2027 holiday lists print 29 October for Tamil Nadu, and the state order is not out as of October 2026. Wish Tamil family on the 28th.

| When in 2027 | Who is celebrating | Line to send | Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages built then (SubhSandesh, n = 89) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two to three days ahead, Mon 25–Tue 26 Oct | Family abroad, anyone posting a card | "Though I am far away, I touch your feet" | 5.6% |
| The evening before, Wed 27 Oct | Households setting alarms for the dawn oil bath | "Anna, this year I'll buy the new clothes" | 27.0% |
| The day, Thu 28 Oct (Tamil Nadu) | Tamil families, from 4 AM | "Amma, Appa, your blessing is all I want" | 49.4% |
| After it has passed, Fri 29 Oct on | North Indian friends still celebrating | "I missed wishing you yesterday" | 11.2% |

The last column is a different festival, so read it as a rough guide. It says half of senders leave it to the day, and a Tamil Deepavali day starts before sunrise.

## Tamil script or Roman? What 17,715 comments show

Every line has Roman letters because many Tamil speakers type that way. In a [2022 study of 17,715 annotated Tamil YouTube comments](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC9271554), Chakravarthi and colleagues report the Tamil comments were code-mixed and typed in Latin script, not Tamil letters.

So match the reader: script for a grandmother who reads Tamil, Roman for a cousin in Toronto who never learned to read it. In a chat, drop the diacritics: vāḻttukaḷ becomes "vazhthukal", with zh for ḻ.

## Putting a Tamil wish on SubhSandesh's Diwali page

A chat line is often enough. For the one person you want to do more for, the [Happy Diwali interactive card on SubhSandesh](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) has a row of wish diyas, each lifting one wish as it is lit, so these lines fit one per diya. It also has a letter in a red-and-gold shagun liffafa and a mithai box that opens onto a Shubh Deepavali card, with love, family and friend modes.

Every line is editable, so you can type Tamil, but we have not tested Tamil fonts on every phone. Press Save, preview on your own phone, then send the private link; it opens in any browser. Shared SubhSandesh pages average 11.1 views each, so it will likely be reopened.

## When a Tamil wish, or a link, is the wrong choice

We checked key words in the *Tamil Lexicon*, not every sentence, and no native speaker has reviewed these lines. If you do not speak Tamil, a wrong pronoun to an elder reads worse than plain English, so have a Tamil speaker check first.

Some people should get a call instead. A grandparent up at 4 AM for the oil bath will remember your voice longer than any card.

No peer-reviewed study of Tamil greeting or blessing forms was found. Searched via findpapers.mjs (Crossref + Europe PMC): "Tamil diglossia spoken written", "Tamil honorific politeness address forms", "Tamil code-mixing romanized social media", plus a Europe PMC query on Tamil AND (diglossia OR code-mixed OR politeness OR honorific). The PMC9271554 corpus paper is about Tamil online writing (script choice is a side observation), which the post uses only for that point. The direction-of-blessing rule is stated from the Lexicon glosses and common usage, not from a cited ethnography.

Tamil wish lines are original; key words verified in the Tamil Lexicon (வாழ்த்து, வாழ்-தல், ஆசி, ஆசீர்வதி-த்தல், நீடூழி, ஒளிர்-தல், விலகு-தல், பெருகு-தல், நட்பு, விளக்கு, தீபம், இனிமை, இனிப்பு, பண்பு, கோலம், தங்கச்சி, நண்பன், பாட்டி, முற்றம், வாசல், வணங்கு-தல், தவறு-தல், அமாவாசை). அகல்விளக்கு, புதுத்துணி and கண்ணு are not Lexicon headwords (compounds/colloquial); grammar of the full sentences not reviewed by a native speaker — disclosed in the body.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the measured top 10, which is mostly undated Tamil-only wish dumps: it is the only page that explains the three grammatical shapes of a Tamil wish and the elder-to-younger direction of a blessing from the Tamil Lexicon, gives every line in script, Roman and English, and times them to the 2027 Tamil Nadu/North India split.
